stories.headline: Trump signals renewed US strikes on Iran as IRGC threatens US bases
stories.summary: Trump said the US has 'knocked the hell out of' Iran and may strike 'a little bit further', while saying the war could end quickly or wind down. The IRGC threatened US bases and Iran warned of wider retaliation. Netanyahu called for regime change, and Trump also said the war would be over very soon.
stories.turkey: A resumed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border, trade and energy security, which is why Ankara is pressing for diplomacy.

stories.headline: Istanbul R4+E3 ministers meet on Hormuz, Yemen, Gaza and Ukraine
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt (R4) and the E3 plus Italy met in Istanbul, hosted by Hakan Fidan. It was the first meeting in this eight-country format. The agenda covered Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab security, Yemen, Palestine and the Russia-Ukraine war. Haaretz reported the aim was a diplomatic alternative to war, with Qatar offering Tehran a non-aggression pact.
stories.turkey: Türkiye is positioning itself as convener between European and Middle Eastern powers on the Iran war and regional crises.

stories.summary: After the Istanbul meeting Fidan said participants agree that a new military attack on Iran would escalate conflicts across the region. He called military intervention no solution and diplomacy the only way out.
stories.turkey: Ankara is publicly aligning eight states against renewed strikes on its neighbour.

stories.headline: Iran claims seven ships hit in Hormuz; Washington and Trump dismiss claims
stories.summary: Iran said its forces hit seven ships in the Strait of Hormuz and warned the US of a wider response. Washington dismissed the claims, and Trump accused Iran of fabricating tanker attack reports to raise oil prices. A tanker was separately hit by an unknown projectile near Oman, and a tanker strike caused an oil spill on UAE beaches. Monitors recorded the most Hormuz-area ship attacks since 2017.
stories.turkey: Disrupted Gulf shipping raises Türkiye's energy import costs and strengthens its case for de-escalation.

stories.summary: US envoy Mike Waltz said Washington is ready for a prolonged conflict and will maintain its blockade of Iranian ports. He said the war continues until a nuclear deal is struck and Iran's enriched stockpile is eliminated. Bessent said US economic pressure has brought oil shipping at Kharg Island to a near standstill.
stories.turkey: A long blockade pushes Iran toward overland routes through Türkiye and its neighbours, increasing Ankara's exposure to sanctions pressure.
